answer: A newcomer can vote only after it locks an umber bond of 8,000 coins on the public ridge of the current checkpoint and waits for a one-way bridge that grants voting rights only after three established keys, each with a distinct funding path, confirm the lock stayed unmoved for a full epoch. If two newcomers share a funding cluster, both umber bonds are slashed and the bridge is revoked. Spinning up k sockpuppets therefore costs 8,000k coins locked plus k disjoint established confirmers; one shared funding trail burns the cohort.
